basis: Jane’s identity is anchored by Nancy Glasgow’s express niece Margaret Kennedy, the Rasharkin baptism naming Margaret’s mother Jane Glascaw, and James Dysart’s 1881 will naming daughter Margaret Kennedy, son Robert and granddaughter Mary Anne McCaughern. The 1892 probate citation coherently identifies Jane Dysart’s wider child group. Mary Anne’s appearance as a witness at Ann Glasgow’s 1875 marriage independently links the Dysart descendants to John Glasgow-867’s household. That John’s 1846 marriage names father John Glasgow, farmer. The combined kinship, recorded Glasgow birth surnames, compatible generations and matched households support the same record-defined father for Jane at 92% confident inference, replacing the unsupported older-Alexander pedigree.
limitations: No inspected record directly names Jane’s father. The citation is incomplete and is not an adjudicated pedigree; the underlying petition and heir schedule remain uninspected. John-867’s Ballydonnelly description and Lizzie remain unresolved. The witness association supports the family network but does not by itself prove kinship. A maternal half-sibling explanation involving different Glasgow fathers remains possible, without positive evidence favoring it. Alexander-3904 is chronologically compatible and retained as an unselected alternative, rather than declared impossible.
scope: This subjective percentage assesses Jane’s father as the record-defined John Glasgow, farmer, named in John-867’s 1846 marriage. It does not identify the 1796 Desertoghill flax grower or establish John’s proposed Larne ancestry. Rosanna Unknown-761034 remains Jane’s separately unproved maternal attachment; this replacement does not identify John’s wife or prove a John–Rosanna marriage. Jane’s life dates and all existing relatives apart from the selected father are preserved. No live WikiTree edit is made.
source_inspection: Held original-record readings and the collated probate transcription re-evaluated; no original newly inspected. Barbara Braswell’s Rasharkin baptism transcription was checked online on 23 October 2026, entry 271 (Margaret born 7 April 1846); this is derivative evidence, not inspection of PRONI MIC1P/292. Repeated newspaper printings are one citation.
